subject: Follow-up: Discovery recap — function calling & JSON output requirements
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Priya Nambiar <priya@healthsecure.io>, DevOps Team <devops@healthsecure.io>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: function calling + structured output needs (summary & next steps)

Hi Priya / HealthSecure team — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call so we’re aligned and can move to a scoped pilot:  

TL;DR: HealthSecure needs deterministic, schema-driven responses for agent workflows (claims triage) with function/tool calling for verification steps. Primary goals are accuracy of structured outputs, low tail-latency for live triage, and tight auditability.

What we heard (pain points):
- Current RAG/chat pipeline returns inconsistent JSON fields and occasionally misses required keys (broken downstream ingestion).
- Tool invocation (callbacks to internal verification service) is brittle — often needs multiple prompt-workarounds.
- Latency spikes during peak hours (~10am–2pm PST) affecting SLA for triage.
- Audit/compliance: need immutable request/response logs and schema versioning for regulatory traceability.

Current stack you described:
- Frontend -> internal API -> RAG pipeline (vector DB + open LLM) -> ingestion to claims workflow.
- Verification service: internal microservice that expects deterministic JSON with exact keys (claim_id, confidence_score, recommended_action, evidence_refs[]).

Success criteria for an initial pilot (agreed):
1) Deterministic JSON output conforming to a supplied schema (pass rate >= 95% for required keys).
2) Function/tool call reliability (>= 98% success for verification invocation).
3) Median token latency < 250ms and P95 < 800ms during test load.
4) End-to-end audit logs retained for 90 days and exportable as NDJSON.

Specific asks on function calling & structured output we captured:
- Schema enforcement: needs both soft (model guidance) and hard (post-response validation + automatic safe fallback) mechanisms.
- Agent workflows: multiple-step flows where the model returns a sequence of actions (call verification, ask clarifying question, emit final JSON). Each action should be addressable and auditable.
- Deterministic formatting: examples and unit-testable prompt/response pairs. You asked for a sample JSON schema and a short set of prompts we can use for regression tests.

Attachments included: one-page summary (healthsecure_mvp_req.pdf) and a starter example schema (example_schema_v1.json).

Proposed next steps (with owners & timing):
- Redwood: provide a tailored pilot plan + ingestion-safe schema adapter (deliver by Tue 24 Feb). (Owner: Soojin)
- HealthSecure: share a 1–2 week representative prompt set and 100 sample messages (anonymized) we can use for regression tests. Also confirm preferred AWS region for private pilot. (Owner: Priya)
- Schedule a 30–45m technical sync between your engineering lead and our solutions engineer to walk the schema+function-call flow. (Owner: Priya/Avery)

Can you confirm these items and share the sample data and preferred time window for the technical sync? Happy to block times next week — we’re flexible.

Thanks,

--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
https://redwood.ai

Attachments (referenced): healthsecure_mvp_req.pdf, example_schema_v1.json
From: Priya Nambiar <priya@healthsecure.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@healthsecure.io>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: function calling + structured output needs (summary & next steps)

Thanks Soojin — this is a solid summary and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications / additions from our side:  

1) Sample data: we can provide 100 anonymized triage transcripts this week. I’ll attach a link to a secure S3 bucket (internal share) — DevOps will send the access info.
2) Schema specifics: the verification microservice expects ISO timestamps and an evidence_refs array with S3 paths (string). The required keys are claim_id, status_code, recommended_action, confidence_score. Any additional metadata is optional.
3) Pilot scope: we want the pilot to cover the most common 3 triage intents (new_claim, escalate, close) + a small set of edge cases. If Redwood can demonstrate 95% pass on required keys across these intents, we’ll greenlight a 3-month POC with reserved capacity.
4) Security/compliance: SOC2 report is required as part of our procurement checklist. Please include SOC2 certificate and a short note on how Redwood handles logs for private deployments.

For the technical sync — our lead engineer (Rahul Shah) is available Wed 25 Feb 10:00–11:30 PST or Thu 26 Feb 13:00–15:00 PST. Could you confirm which slot works for your team?

I’ll ask DevOps to send the S3 access and a short list of sample prompts (they’ll anonymize PHI).

Best,
Priya
Head of Product Operations | HealthSecure
priya@healthsecure.io
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: function calling + structured output needs (summary & next steps)

Hi Priya — thanks for the clarifications. Quick notes from the solutions engineering side:  

- We’ll bring Chloe to the technical sync to walk through schema enforcement options (prompt-level + post-parse validator + automatic fallback variant).
- For deterministic outputs we recommend a two-layer approach: (1) response shaping with a strongly-typed schema in the prompt + few-shot examples; (2) a lightweight validator that rewrites or routes to a fallback model when the response doesn't pass. We’ll demonstrate both during the sync.
- On SOC2: I’ll attach a short SOC2 summary and our compliance contact info to the follow-up (we’ll include how logs are captured when running Redwood Private).

Avery — on availability: Wed 25 Feb 10:00–11:30 PST works for us. I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda and required pre-reads.

Cheers,
Avery

avery.johnson@redwood.com

- Share starter regression harness with example prompts + evaluation script (I’ve attached example_schema_v1.json — please review and let us know schema quirks).

Looking forward to the sync.
